analysis_title: Floor Guard AI — Comprehensive Root Cause Forensics (Vectors A through M)

A_dataset_quality.detail: Legacy archives contained synthetic samples with uncalibrated color saturations and lack of real-world curled mat / cracked tile images.

B_annotations.detail: Legacy dataset remapped loose mats (class 7) and floor cracks (class 8/9) into obstacle_debris (class 5), causing semantic dilution and misclassification.

C_duplicates.detail: 445 exact bit duplicates and 435 perceptual duplicates existed across raw and split folders, causing model over-memorization on duplicate backgrounds.

D_model_architecture.detail: Ultralytics YOLOv8s with 11.15M parameters is optimal for fast CPU/edge inference (180ms) and high multi-hazard recall.

E_wrong_checkpoint_loading.detail: Fast inference daemon previously held an older weights file in RAM until process restart. Synchronized to models/floorguard_yolo.pt.

F_class_mapping_mismatch.detail: Predict_video.py had a 10-class map that lacked floor_mat_hazard and floor_damage, forcing cracks and curled mats into water_spill. Upgraded to Canonical 12-Hazard Universal Mapping.

G_image_preprocessing_mismatch.detail: Direct OpenCV BGR vs PIL RGB conversion was inconsistent across montage and full-frame paths; standard RGB normalized arrays enforced.

H_confidence_thresholds.detail: Hardcoded min threshold of 0.30 in predict_image.py discarded genuine low-contrast liquid pools and curled edges, defaulting to Clean Floor.

I_bbox_coordinate_conversion.detail: Out-of-bounds boundary check (by + bh <= img.shape[0]) failed when boxes touched pixel margins by 1px, skipping semantic validation entirely.

J_video_frame_sampling.detail: Video analyzer took only 8 rigid fixed segments, skipping short-duration hazards and jumping past transition points.

K_temporal_tracking.detail: Spatial IoU threshold in temporal event consolidation was 0.15, which separated moving camera frames into duplicate event alerts.

L_frontend_stale_state.detail: Frontend React state maintained static demo preset values when server response was delayed; resolved by active mode isolation.

M_keyframe_sync.detail: seekTime was recorded as start_sec while frame was extracted at mid_sec, creating player vs thumbnail timestamp desynchronization.

investigation_verdict: The failures did not stem from a single module, but from an interaction between duplicate training data, class remapping omission, boundary-rejection filters in predict_image.py, and seekTime desynchronization in predict_video.py.
